summary.headline: The Affordable Housing Trust advanced a draft senior housing zoning bylaw and approved moving town housing funds into an interest-bearing account.
summary.summary: The Affordable Housing Trust reviewed draft zoning changes for 55-plus housing, favoring an option allowing up to eight units per acre on two-acre lots with a 12.5 percent affordability requirement. Members learned that roughly one million dollars in trust funds held in a zero-interest account will be shifted to a savings program earning about 3.5 percent. The board also voted to request the Select Board authorize dedicated web pages to promote trust initiatives and solicit land donations, and agreed to confer with the Planning Board and Zoning Board of Appeals in late fall.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The trust reviewed and approved open session minutes from its meeting on September 23, 2026.
key_details: Approved minutes of September 23, 2026 by a 3-0 vote.

topics.title: Special Town Meeting recap
topics.summary: Members discussed the results of Special Town Meeting, focusing on the defeat of the two-family housing zoning article, which gained a majority (85-80) but failed to achieve the required two-thirds threshold. Members noted voter confusion and emphasized the ongoing need for public education regarding affordable and diverse housing options. The trust also noted Community Preservation Act funding dynamics, including large unallocated reserve balances.
key_details: Two-family bylaw failed at Town Meeting, voting 85 in favor and 80 opposed, short of two-thirds.
Members discussed potential access to unallocated Community Preservation Act funds beyond the statutory 10 percent housing reserve.
Roughly $376,000 represented the unallocated 70 percent CPA bucket in the prior year.

topics.title: Regional affordable housing trust meeting
topics.summary: A member reported on a regional meeting in Sudbury convened by the Metropolitan Area Planning Council for municipal affordable housing trusts. Topics included Acton's collaboration between housing and open space committees, Sudbury's nine-member trust with dedicated municipal staff support, and Concord's practice of allocating roughly 36 percent of local Community Preservation Act funds to housing.
key_details: Sudbury operates a nine-member affordable housing trust with municipal staff assistance.
Statewide average for Community Preservation Act fund allocation to housing is approximately 36 percent, well above the statutory 10 percent minimum.
Members discussed exploring a local bylaw or formal agreement for annual transfers from CPA reserves to the trust.
topics.outcome: Trust agreed to explore bylaw or CPC request mechanisms with town counsel.

topics.title: Senior housing zoning bylaw update
topics.summary: The trust reviewed a drafted zoning amendment updating bylaws for independent senior multifamily housing (ages 55 and older), removing the town-wide 7 percent cap on elderly housing units. The trust reached consensus on Option 2, setting a minimum lot size of two acres, maximum density of eight units per acre, and a 12.5 percent affordable unit mandate, while discussing fractional payment alternatives and enforcement.
key_details: Replaces existing multifamily housing for the elderly bylaw with independent senior housing for ages 55 and older.
Removes the existing 7 percent cap on total elderly units allowed in Southborough.
Option 2 establishes a two-acre minimum lot size, maximum density of eight units per acre, and a 12.5 percent affordability requirement.
On a two-acre parcel, Option 2 allows up to 16 units, including two affordable units.
Next steps involve presenting the draft to the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, and Select Board in late November or early December.
topics.outcome: Trust reached consensus to support Option 2 and will present the draft to other municipal boards.
topics.why_it_matters: Changes rules for senior housing developments in town, potentially allowing higher density and creating more age-restricted and deed-restricted affordable housing.

topics.title: Trust fund banking and investment update
topics.summary: A member reported that approximately one million dollars in housing trust funds had historically been held in a zero-interest account. Working with the town treasurer, the trust arranged to move the balance into a fully insured savings program spread across sister savings banks, earning approximately 3.5 percent annual interest.
key_details: The trust currently holds approximately $1 million in cash assets.
Funds will earn roughly 3.5 percent interest, yielding an estimated $35,000 annually.
Full balance is covered under FDIC and SBLIC insurance through participating institutions.
topics.outcome: Town treasurer moved funds to the interest-bearing program.
topics.why_it_matters: Generates roughly $35,000 per year in interest income for the town to put toward affordable housing initiatives.

topics.title: CPA application and MassHousing technical assistance
topics.summary: Members received an update on the technical review of their Community Preservation Act funding application by the Community Preservation Committee, noting minor questions regarding survey data. Members also recapped an initial meeting held on October 16 with MassHousing Partnership staff regarding municipal technical assistance, operational manuals, and project financing.
key_details: Community Preservation Committee completed a technical review of the trust application with minor questions.
Trust leaders met with MassHousing Partnership on October 16 to explore technical assistance and financial toolkits.
topics.outcome: Staff and members will provide updated survey data to the Community Preservation Committee.

topics.title: Outreach and web presence for property donations
topics.summary: Members discussed outreach strategies to encourage landowners to donate property or development rights for affordable housing. The trust voted to request that the Select Board approve adding or updating content on the town website to publicize the trust's mission, provide housing education, and solicit potential property donations.
key_details: Promotional flyers distributed at Heritage Day generated little public response.
Select Board meets November 4, where the website request could be considered.
The board discussed drafting a formal letter from the chair to the Select Board.
topics.outcome: Motion approved 4-0 to request Select Board authorization for housing trust web pages.

topics.title: Parcel screening and executive session
topics.summary: The trust discussed potential methods to identify parcels suitable for affordable housing, including using town assessor records and street lists. Members cautioned against overly intrusive public data searches for potential donors. At the end of the meeting, the trust voted to enter executive session to discuss potential property acquisitions.
key_details: Evaluated using assessor databases and town clerk street lists to screen large parcels.
Voted to enter executive session under M.G.L. Chapter 30A, Section 21(a)(6) to discuss potential property acquisition.
topics.outcome: Voted 5-0 to enter executive session with no intent to return to open session.
topics.why_it_matters: Town acquisition of land directly affects municipal land inventory, spending, and future site selection for affordable housing developments.

votes.motion: Authorize the chair to send a letter requesting the Select Board support modifying the town website to include pages dedicated to the Affordable Housing Trust, its activities, public education, and soliciting property donations.
Enter executive session under M.G.L. Chapter 30A, Section 21(a)(6) to discuss potential property acquisition without returning to open session.

public_comment.summary: A resident and former civil engineer stated he was attending for the first time to get up to speed on the proposed 55-plus zoning bylaw and two-family housing, noting his past involvement with a local Chapter 40B review.

upcoming.what: Select Board meeting where the website request may be considered
Meetings with the Planning Board and Zoning Board of Appeals to present the draft 55-plus bylaw
